articles.title: New Withings accounts face a subscription requirement for data sharing
articles.dek: Home Assistant’s setup guide flags the change; Withings says accounts created before October 12 are unaffected.
body: Withings says its free API plan introduces a Withings+ subscription requirement for new accounts sharing their data. Home Assistant’s setup guide adds the subscription as a prerequisite, changing the cost of connecting newly created Withings accounts through the existing setup process.

Withings dates the policy change to October 12 and says accounts created before that date are unaffected. The policy covers free-plan applications already in operation as well as new ones. Ethan G adds the warning in his first contribution to Home Assistant’s website.

pullRequests.title: Add Withings+ prerequisite for new accounts

articles.title: Home Assistant pairs LaMetric displays with a button press
articles.dek: Compatible devices share their access key locally, without a LaMetric account.
body: Home Assistant adds a local setup route for LaMetric displays: confirm the device, then press its top button to authorize the connection. Compatible devices from 2022 onward provide their access key directly, avoiding a LaMetric account or manually copying the key.

Franck Nijhof tests the full connection on a LaMetric TIME. The display asks for a press only after the person confirms its address, with a minute to respond. Older devices keep the cloud-import and manual-key options, and the local route also supports replacing rejected credentials.

pullRequests.title: Add setting up LaMetric with a press on its button
Document setting up LaMetric with a press on its button

articles.title: ESPHome gives voice-device makers a faster wake-word option
articles.dek: An optional memory setting reduces recognition processing time in a measured ESP32 test.
body: ESPHome lets makers place active wake-word models in faster internal memory, reducing the processing time needed to listen for a wake word. The option starts off and falls back to the existing memory arrangement when there is not enough internal space.

In contributor embe’s test on an ESP32-WROVER with one 16 kHz model, each processing call fell from about 13.3 milliseconds to 3.7 milliseconds. A separate playback test reduced wake-word processing from about 64% to 33% of one core. Those measurements describe that device and model.

Only active models use the extra memory, including models loaded while the device is running. Disabling a model releases it again. The change speeds model processing; it does not establish better recognition accuracy. This is embe’s first contribution to ESPHome, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

pullRequests.title: [micro_wake_word] Add opt-in internal RAM placement

articles.title: Music Assistant blocks an image route into Home Assistant data
articles.dek: The picture loader stops carrying its Home Assistant access token to unrelated API paths.
body: Music Assistant restricts its Home Assistant picture loader after finding that a client could use it to read other Home Assistant API responses. The loader previously fetched any path registered as an image with Music Assistant’s Home Assistant access token and returned the response.

Marvin Schenkel limits requests to the paths used for entity pictures, rejects attempts to traverse into other paths, and requires an image response no larger than 10 MiB. OzGav reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Limit the Home Assistant image proxy to entity pictures

articles.title: Home Assistant reads UniFi Alarm Hub wired zones
articles.dek: Configured inputs, tamper detection and backup-battery status join the existing alarm controls.
body: Home Assistant adds the UniFi Alarm Hub as a device and exposes its configured wired zones. Inputs can report motion, an opening, smoke, glass breakage or an emergency button according to their configured zone type, allowing the hub’s signals to participate in household automations.

The connection also exposes tamper detection, backup-battery voltage and problems, and the last event time. Follow-up corrections handle hubs added while Home Assistant is running and hubs without a name. Arming and disarming use the existing alarm control panel; the addition does not control the hub’s siren outputs.

pullRequests.title: Add UniFi Alarm Hub support to UniFi Protect
Fix UniFi Protect alarm hubs added at runtime and without a name

articles.title: Home Assistant repairs nine connections without rebuilding their setup
articles.dek: Rejected passwords and access keys prompt for replacements while keeping the existing integration.
body: Home Assistant adds credential-replacement flows to nine integrations, letting people replace a rejected password or access key while preserving the existing connection. The additions cover Bond, Dexcom, Kodi, Kostal Plenticore, Nexia, Pushbullet, Rachio, Slack and Smart Meter Texas.

G Johansson’s forms ask for the credentials each service needs and preserve the existing connection. Slack, Pushbullet and Nexia check that the replacement still belongs to the same workspace, account or house; Bond checks the hub. Smart Meter Texas also starts recovery when authentication fails during normal meter readings.

articles.title: Home Assistant reconnects cameras and recordings from motionEye 0.44
articles.dek: The connection follows the camera server’s new sign-in method and preserves seeking through saved videos.
body: Home Assistant adapts its motionEye connection to the session-based sign-in introduced in motionEye 0.44. Live camera views, current snapshots and saved images and movies use the authenticated connection instead of relying on the older signed addresses.

Marcin Krawczyk reports validation with twelve cameras on motionEye 0.44.0 and Home Assistant 2026.9.1, including live previews, saved photographs and playback of two test recordings. Saved movies stream through Home Assistant and preserve the requests needed for seeking. This is his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: motioneye: support motionEye 0.44 session authentication

articles.title: ESPHome keeps serial input from repeatedly restarting ESP8266 devices
articles.dek: Slower serial connections stop blocking the Wi-Fi work needed to keep the device running.
body: ESPHome changes how ESP8266 boards receive software-driven serial data so the incoming bytes do not hold up Wi-Fi long enough to restart the device. The correction applies at 19,200 baud and below; faster connections keep the existing method.

J. Nick Koston reproduced the problem on a D1 mini receiving serial data while repeatedly reconnecting an encrypted client. At 19,200 baud, the old version restarted three times in four minutes. The revised version ran the same setup without a reset at 9,600 and 19,200 baud, although some byte errors remained during reconnect bursts.

pullRequests.title: [uart] Stop ESP8266 software serial RX ISR from blocking for a whole byte

articles.title: A week of clearer automations, guided device setup and smarter music
articles.dek: October 5–11 connected individual improvements into more complete ways to troubleshoot, build and listen.
body: From Monday, October 5 through Sunday, October 11, Home Assistant connected more of the steps in troubleshooting an automation, ESPHome extended device setup, and Music Assistant paired richer playback with lower storage and processing costs.

Home Assistant’s automation changes connect testing with diagnosis. Disabled steps can be tried without enabling them in ordinary runs; a trace links to the exact script it started; and failures in 20 integrations reach the caller instead of appearing successful. Together, the week’s work makes it easier to distinguish a step that was skipped, a child routine that ran and a command that failed.

ESPHome’s setup work covers different points in a device’s life. Ready-made images and serial Wi-Fi setup broaden the browser route for seven Beken, Lightning and Realtek chip types. Signed devices get an explicit USB route for their first custom installation, while device-defined setup pages let makers explain settings and ask owners to choose household entities. The latter requires Home Assistant 2026.11; it is separate from firmware installation.

Music Assistant pairs richer transitions with lower costs for large collections. Its audio-analysis storage becomes smaller and separate from the music library, long shuffled queues are ordered in manageable batches, and Smart Fades gain transitions for songs that cannot share a beat. The combined direction matters for people who want an ordinary mixed collection to play smoothly without making its size a burden.

articles.title: Home Assistant restores speech from Gemini 3.8
articles.dek: Speech generation no longer fails after Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS has already produced its answer.
body: Home Assistant accepts the complete WAV speech files returned by Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS. Its existing converter expected raw audio samples and rejected the new file format, so an otherwise successful generation could still produce no speech.

The change keeps complete files intact while preserving conversion for older raw-audio responses. It also avoids sending sampling and thinking settings that newer Gemini models do not support, while retaining saved preferences for older models. Contributor oohhddaanngg verifies a live WAV response through the corrected speech entity in their first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Handle Gemini generation parameters and complete WAV TTS responses

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps Rituals controls working through sensor failures
articles.dek: Less frequent cloud checks also cut one diffuser’s requests from about 100 to 14 an hour.
body: Home Assistant separates Rituals Perfume Genie controls from its sensor checks, so a failed battery or cartridge request no longer takes the diffuser’s controls offline or prevents setup. All an account’s diffusers are checked together every five minutes; slower-changing readings use longer intervals.

Franck Nijhof calculates about fourteen requests an hour for one diffuser instead of about one hundred, with each extra diffuser adding two rather than another hundred. Battery and connection readings update hourly, while cartridge fill updates daily or when the cartridge changes. Existing entity identifiers stay the same.

articles.title: ESPHome gives Daikin controls presets and half-degree temperatures
articles.dek: Infrared controls follow the remote’s comfort choices and its automatic end to boost mode.
body: ESPHome adds boost, sleep, eco, comfort and activity presets to compatible Daikin infrared air-conditioner controls, along with temperature choices in half-degree Celsius steps. Receiving a command from the original remote updates the selected preset too.

Contributor opcod3 makes boost return to the ordinary setting after 20 minutes, matching the end of the unit’s powerful mode. That timing follows changes made through ESPHome, the remote and settings restored when the device starts. This is opcod3’s first ESPHome contribution, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

articles.title: Home Assistant opens Dropbox backup lists faster
articles.dek: Downloading several small metadata files together cuts a measured 30-backup wait from 23 seconds to 3.4.
body: Home Assistant fetches Dropbox backup details eight at a time instead of waiting for each download before starting the next. In Ruslan Sayfutdinov’s test with thirty backups, collecting that metadata took 3.4 seconds instead of 23 seconds.

The change speeds the backup list, including the backups page. It does not change backup creation or restoration; limiting concurrency to eight avoids sending an unbounded batch of requests to Dropbox.

pullRequests.title: Download Dropbox backup metadata concurrently

articles.title: Home Assistant automations can use a fresh KNX reply
articles.dek: A read action returns the requested value instead of only sending a request onto the control network.
body: Home Assistant’s KNX read action can return a reply directly to an automation. That gives the following steps a fresh value from a chosen group address instead of only sending a request onto the building’s control network.

The reply can include a decoded value, unit and sending device when the loaded KNX project describes them, alongside the raw message. The action waits up to two seconds and reports an error if no answer arrives. Returning data supports one address at a time; ordinary requests to one or several addresses continue to work.

articles.title: Home Assistant controls SwitchBot’s Circulator Fan Pro
articles.dek: The Bluetooth fan gains speed, oscillation and preset controls alongside its two-level night light.
body: Home Assistant adds the SwitchBot Circulator Fan Pro W1160 through its encrypted Bluetooth connection. Its fan controls cover speed, oscillation and device-provided presets, including hurricane mode.
The same device exposes a high-or-low night light and a separate vertical-oscillation switch. The SwitchBot team reports testing the implementation on physical hardware.

articles.title: Music Assistant’s AirPlay tool lets older Apple TVs play again
articles.dek: A public device key no longer causes an unnecessary demand for a pairing secret.
body: Music Assistant’s AirPlay tool stops refusing older Apple TVs that allow unpaired playback. A device such as Apple TV 2 could be rejected before the connection even started because its advertised public key was mistaken for a requirement to pair.

Marvin Schenkel removes that initial check. Devices that require pairing still reject an unpaired connection themselves. The source identifies this as a regression from playback that worked in Music Assistant 2.9; Marcel van der Veldt reviewed the correction.
